Then the pivot: low-ticket pricing can no longer be maintained — "Protecting the alpha is becoming the new priority." **"The War Room will become an exclusive, high-ticket channel, with no new entries for future members."**

## Why it matters

- The series arc completes into pricing discipline: free Substack firehose (400+ strategies "in the past few days") as top-of-funnel → War Room converts to high-ticket → door closes. This is the classic creator-economics sequence, executed on top of the research corpus this series has tracked.
- What's new for the standing decision: a **claimed deadline**. The 11-10 join-or-not task (Tasks/Inbox.md) was "decide ahead of the 900-strategy code drop" — this tweet says the drop's home goes exclusive "with no new entries for future members." If joining was ever live, the window now carries a marketing-imposed cap (amended onto the existing task, no new task filed).
- The four charts quietly reconfirm the series' own numbers: labeled Sharpe range 0.71–1.12, median ~0.95 — the same "~0.9 costs-in fleet" picture from the 11-10 note. The best chart (1.12) is the only one with no OCR-recoverable strategy label; the only chart admitting "before costs" (p3) is also the weakest (0.71).
- Skepticism gates: the receipts gap is unchanged — author-run Python tests, offline numbers, author-labeled, no third-party verification (contrast [[2026-11-09-milk-man-po10-extreme-full-receipts]]). "Only 1% of everything I've shared" is unfalsifiable marketing arithmetic; "backtests to 1980" spans four decades of regime change but stays in-sample; and "no new entries" is a textbook urgency close — treat the deadline as marketing pressure until the door observably shuts.
